The phrase "It pays the bills" is a common idiom used to indicate that a job provides sufficient income for basic living expenses but is not necessarily a source of great passion, prestige, or high financial reward. By using this understated description, Henry likely intends to downplay the significance or personal fulfillment he derives from his current role, possibly to avoid appearing boastful or to signal modesty. Furthermore, by immediately steering the conversation toward industry trends, Henry demonstrates a pragmatic communicative intention to shift the focus from personal details to professional or intellectual topics. This suggests he may be uncomfortable discussing his personal career satisfaction, wishes to maintain a professional distance, or is more interested in engaging with the broader context of the industry than in sharing personal anecdotes. The overall effect is a polite deflection of personal inquiry while maintaining engagement through a relevant, neutral topic.

The capital of France is Paris.
